samples.summary: No test covers that COOKIE_SECURE now decides `cliLoginAvailable` — the CLI consent gate on a plain-http, non-loopback origin
samples.evidence: `cliLoginAvailable` (github-auth.guard.ts:215) is `secureCookies(...) || loopbackCallback(...)`, so the new `COOKIE_SECURE` short-circuit in `secureCookies` (line 159-160) newly makes a CLI login startable on a plain-http non-loopback origin (COOKIE_SECURE=true) and newly *refuses* one on an https origin (COOKIE_SECURE=false). The existing gate tests use only `insecureConfig()`/`httpsConfig()` (spec lines 444-466, 686-700); the three new COOKIE_SECURE tests assert only `secureCookies()`'s return, `loginCookieName`, and the web state cookie's `secure` option. Nothing exercises `canActivate` with a CLI query under an overridden config, so a regression in either direction of that gate would pass green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. cliLoginAvailable (github-auth.guard.ts:215-217) is `secureCookies() || loopbackCallback()`, and secureCookies (158-160) now short-circuits on the new COOKIE_SECURE override, so that variable newly decides whether canActivate throws 'Command-line sign-in requires an https server' (guard.ts:507-518): CLI startable on a plain-http non-loopback origin with COOKIE_SECURE=true, and refused on an https origin with COOKIE_SECURE=false. Searching all *.ts repo-wide, the only test occurrences of COOKIE_SECURE are the three new tests at spec:730, 752, 768 (plus the warning-string assertion at 796). Test 730 does call canActivate but with contextFor({}) — a web request with no mode=cli — asserting only the state cookie's `secure` option; 752 and 768 assert only secureCookies()/loginCookieName() and never build a request. The two CLI-gate tests (spec:444-454 using insecureConfig(), spec:459-466 loopback) supply no COOKIE_SECURE. No test anywhere asserts the 400 message: grep for 'requires an https server' finds only guard.ts:516, backend/README.md:116 and self-hosting.md:129. auth.controller.spec.ts (its only overridden-config test, 716-741, is a logout/clearCookie case), github.strategy.spec.ts, cli-auth.store.spec.ts and packages/backend/test/*.e2e-spec.ts contain no COOKIE_SECURE. No counterexample found: a regression in either direction of the CLI availability gate would pass green, so this is a new behavior branch shipped without a meaningful test.

finding.summary: New user-facing login error banner (`?error=login_state` → mapped message, plus fallback) has no test at all
finding.evidence: login-form.tsx now reads `useSearchParams()` and renders a `role="alert"` div using ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR. This is the only feedback a user gets when the OAuth callback refuses their login (the backend redirects to `/login?error=login_state`). Frontend has a running vitest lane with many component tests (e.g. packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/datasource-dialog.test.tsx, app/files/__tests__/generic-file-view.test.tsx), but there is no test file for login-form or the login page — a regression that dropped the banner or the fallback mapping would ship silently.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new login error banner has no test at all. A dedicated test file exists at packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/login-form.test.tsx — the reviewer's globs (src/components/*.test.tsx does not descend into __tests__/) missed it, despite the finding itself citing datasource-dialog.test.tsx from that same directory. The test renders the real LoginForm inside a real MemoryRouter driven by the actual URL query string; useSearchParams is NOT mocked, so there is no over-mocking. It covers all three branches of the new behavior: (1) lines 21-28 assert no role="alert" is present without ?error, plus the GitHub link renders; (2) lines 30-41 assert the ?error=login_state alert text contains "expired" and "try again", matching ERROR_MESSAGES.login_state at login-form.tsx:14-15, and that the retry link survives the error; (3) lines 43-50 exact-match the fallback alert text to "Sign-in did not complete. Please try again.", identical to FALLBACK_ERROR at login-form.tsx:18, and further assert the raw unknown code is not echoed back. These assertions are behavior-dependent, not vacuous: removing the {error && ...} block at login-form.tsx:43-50 fails tests 2 and 3, and breaking the ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR mapping at line 48 fails test 2 or 3 depending on direction — exactly the regressions the finding says would ship silently. The test is genuinely executed by the frontend vitest lane: vite.config.ts:268 includes "src/**/*.test.tsx" which matches this path, with environment "jsdom" (line 267) and setupFiles tests/setup.ts (line 269). The finding's factual premise is false against this working tree.
